video.transcriptSummary: This practical operational walkthrough configures Google Antigravity across Desktop 2.0, IDE, and the agy CLI for both Engineering and Content teams. We establish bounded autonomy via proceed-in-sandbox and command allowlists/denylists, master all 5 customization primitives (Rules, Skills, Plugins, Hooks, MCP Servers) within the 24 KB per-file / 20,000-token aggregate budget, scaffold starter AGENTS.md and editorial-qa workflows, connect least-privilege Streamable HTTP MCP servers, package org-wide Git-symlinked plugins, and conclude with daily context-hygiene habits and a Day-1 teammate onboarding smoke test.

steps.title: Architecture at a Glance: Surfaces & 5-Tier Context Precedence
steps.summary: Treat AI configuration like infrastructure-as-code: safe global defaults, specialized rules per repository, and repeatable workflows packaged as Skills and Plugins. Match each task to Antigravity 2.0 Desktop, IDE, or agy CLI.
keyTakeaways: Antigravity 2.0 Desktop excels at multi-task orchestration, parallel projects, Scheduled Tasks, and Auxiliary Pane monitoring (Subagents, Artifacts, Files Changed).
Antigravity IDE excels at deep hands-on coding with Tab/Supercomplete, Tab-to-Jump, Tab-to-Import, Cmd+I / Ctrl+I Inline Command, Code Lenses, and Diagnostic Auto-Fix.
Antigravity CLI (agy) powers fast terminal sessions, headless CI scripts, and plugin enable/disable commands via ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json.
Discovery precedence flows strictly: 1. Workspace (.agents/ + AGENTS.md) -> 2. Declared Repo Configs -> 3. Global (~/.gemini/config/) -> 4. Built-ins -> 5. Global Declared Configs.
actionChecklist: Install and authenticate across Antigravity 2.0 Desktop, Antigravity IDE, and the agy CLI.
Confirm which surface fits each part of your workflow (IDE for localized diffs; Desktop 2.0 for swarms & schedules; CLI for headless automation).
Verify live customization discovery in Skills & Customizations or via agy /help.

steps.title: Baseline Security, Permissions & Bounded Autonomy
steps.summary: Configure Global Settings once to achieve bounded autonomy and Day 4 Security Guardrails — lights-out speed on safe local verification loops while enforcing Human-Lit approval for auth, security, finance, secrets, and outbound actions.
keyTakeaways: Set Global Tool Execution Policy to proceed-in-sandbox with Terminal Sandbox Enabled to contain filesystem and network side effects; set Non-Workspace File Access and Internet Access Policy to ask (or deny on strict repos).

Configure Command Allowlist for safe local loops (git status, git diff, git log, npm test, pytest, tsc --noEmit), Command Denylist for destructive ops (rm -rf, git push --force, git reset --hard, DROP TABLE), and Browser Allowlist to restrict origins on sensitive repos while staying open for editorial research.

Apply Selective Autonomy Delegation Boundaries: docs, unit tests, lint fixes, and validated JSON bundles can run lights-out; authentication, security/RLS, finance, hooks, and infra access must remain Human-Lit.
Pair hooks/hitl-gate.py (PreToolUse run_command force_ask) with hooks/secret-guard.py (PreToolUse edit_file/write_file secret & credential leak hard-deny).
Use Settings -> Project Settings for repo-specific overrides (e.g., request-review for Terraform/infra repos; open web access on editorial research workspaces) rather than weakening global defaults.
actionChecklist: Lock Tool Execution Policy = proceed-in-sandbox, Terminal Sandbox = Enabled, Non-Workspace File Access = ask, and Internet Access Policy = ask in Global Settings.
Configure Command Allowlist (git status, git diff, git log, npm test, pytest, tsc --noEmit) and Command Denylist (rm -rf, git push --force, git reset --hard, DROP TABLE).
Configure Browser Allowlist (restrict origins on sensitive production repos; allow research domains on content workspaces).
Enable Notifications and Keep Awake when running /goal or parallel swarms, and set stricter Project-Level Overrides on production/infra repos.

steps.title: Master the 5 Customization Primitives & Context Budget
steps.summary: Choose the exact customization primitive for each job so you never bloat the model's context window or fight drifting instructions.
keyTakeaways: Rules (AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md) walk up from CWD to .git root, load always-on, and are capped at 24 KB per file and 20,000 aggregate tokens (over-budget rules demote to path pointers).
Skills (.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md) use progressive disclosure: only name + description load upfront; bulky reference manuals belong in skills/<name>/references/.
Plugins bundle rules, skills, subagents, hooks, and MCP servers into one toggleable unit (~/.gemini/config/plugins/<name>/).
Hooks (.agents/hooks.json or plugin-root hooks.json) enforce deterministic code guardrails (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) that natural-language rules cannot guarantee.
MCP Servers connect external tools (GitHub, Databases, Google Workspace, Cloud, CMS) globally or scoped to a plugin.
actionChecklist: Keep root AGENTS.md crisp (~2–8 KB of hard invariants, no YAML frontmatter).
Move multi-step runbooks and checklists out of AGENTS.md into progressive-disclosure SKILL.md folders.
Audit total rules size to stay comfortably inside the 24 KB file cap and 20,000-token budget.

steps.title: Configure Your Engineering Workspace & Fail-Closed Hooks
steps.summary: Commit AGENTS.md, .memory/, plans/, and .agents/hooks.json directly into every engineering repo so every teammate gets identical quality gates immediately on git clone.
keyTakeaways: Standalone AGENTS.md files use plain Markdown (no YAML frontmatter) listing Source-of-Truth commands, Architecture Boundaries (domain/api/ui), and Non-Negotiable Invariants.
Hook payloads use camelCase JSON on stdin/stdout (toolCall.args.CommandLine, conversationId).
CRITICAL: PreToolUse fails closed on {} — your hook script MUST always emit an explicit decision (allow, ask, force_ask, or deny).
In Stop hooks, always check continuationActive to prevent infinite loops; in native plugins, hooks.json MUST sit at the plugin root.
Install Marketplace engineering plugins (Cloudflare, Vercel, Supabase, Chrome DevTools, Figma, Jira/ClickUp) via Customizations -> Marketplace.
actionChecklist: Commit starter AGENTS.md with exact install, typecheck, lint, test, and build commands.
Register PreToolUse HITL safety gate in .agents/hooks.json (or install the global code-factory plugin).
Install and authenticate core infrastructure & browser QA Marketplace plugins.

additionalCodeSnippets.code:
# Engineering Rules — <Project Name>

## 1. Commands (Source of Truth)
- Install: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- Typecheck: `pnpm typecheck`
- Lint: `pnpm lint`
- Unit Tests: `pnpm test`
- Build: `pnpm build`

## 2. Architecture & Boundaries
- `src/domain/`: Pure business logic. Zero framework or DB imports.
- `src/api/`: Boundary layer. Validate all external payloads with Zod before calling domain services.
- `src/ui/`: Design tokens only; no raw hex values or magic pixel offsets.

## 3. Non-Negotiable Invariants
- **Security:** Never hardcode secrets. Parameterized queries only. Enforce auth/RLS on every new route/table.
- **Reliability:** Explicit timeouts (<= 5000ms) on outbound HTTP calls. Paginate all list endpoints (default 20, max 100).
- **Testing:** Every new domain module or bug fix requires deterministic unit tests (mock only external I/O).
- **Verification:** Run `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` before claiming completion.

steps.title: Configure Content & Editorial Workspaces with Rigor
steps.summary: Content projects fail when driven by ad-hoc chat prompts. Apply engineering discipline to editorial repos with versioned voice rules, gold-standard examples, verified product facts, and a decoupled editorial-qa review skill.
keyTakeaways: Structure content repos with AGENTS.md (voice, ICP, banned clichés, factual attribution), content-briefs/, drafts/, published/, and .agents/skills/{draft-longform,editorial-qa,repurpose-kit}/.
Store 2–3 canonical A+ pieces inside skills/draft-longform/examples/ and verified claims inside references/product-facts.md.
Enforce factual invariants: never invent benchmarks or quotes; mark unverified claims with [VERIFY: <what to check>].
Run editorial-qa in a fresh subagent context so the reviewer audits accuracy, voice, and structure objectively.
Connect Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Canva, Figma, and ClickUp via Agent Marketplace.
actionChecklist: Create an editorial AGENTS.md defining primary reader, voice, banned buzzwords, and citation rules.
Add .agents/skills/editorial-qa/SKILL.md with the 4-stage Accuracy -> Voice -> Structure -> Verdict rubric.
Install Google Workspace (Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides) and Canva/Figma Marketplace plugins.

codeSnippet.code:
---
name: editorial-qa
description: >-
  Use when reviewing, editing, or finalizing any article, newsletter, docs page,
  or script before publication to verify brand voice, factual accuracy, clarity,
  and formatting compliance.
---

# Editorial QA Pass

Run this 4-stage audit in a fresh subagent context:
1. **Accuracy Audit:** Flag every metric, date, quote, or claim missing a verified source.
2. **Voice & Cliche Pass:** Compare against style-guide.md; cut filler intros and hedging.
3. **Structure & Readability:** Verify scannable headers, <= 4-line paragraphs, and clear CTA.
4. **Output:** Return Blocking Issues, Line Edits, and Ready / Needs Revision verdict.

additionalCodeSnippets.code:
# Editorial & Brand Rules — <Brand / Team Name>

## 1. Audience & Voice
- **Primary Reader:** Engineering leaders and senior builders (skeptical of hype; value concrete tradeoffs).
- **Voice:** Direct, crisp, evidence-backed, practitioner-to-practitioner.
- **Banned Patterns:** Never use filler intros ("In today's fast-paced world..."), vague buzzwords ("game-changer", "delve", "unlock"), or unverified statistics.

## 2. Factual & Attribution Invariants
- Never invent customer quotes, benchmarks, or citations. Mark unverified claims with `[VERIFY: <what to check>]`.
- Every external statistic must include source name, year, and URL.

## 3. Structural Standards
- Lead with the takeaway or concrete problem in the first 3 lines.
- Use scannable H2/H3 headers, short paragraphs (<= 4 lines), tables for comparisons, and concrete examples.
- End every piece with a single clear next action or takeaway.

steps.title: Connect MCP Servers & Distribute Org-Wide Team Plugins
steps.summary: Stop copy-pasting prompts in Slack. Connect least-privilege Streamable HTTP MCP servers cleanly and distribute rules, skills, personas, and hooks via Git-backed team plugins.
keyTakeaways: Prefer Streamable HTTP (url ending in /mcp) for remote MCP servers; wrap legacy HTTP+SSE (/sse) servers with a stdio bridge such as mcp-remote.
Prefix every plugin MCP server name (e.g., acme-cms, not cms) because MCP server names share a single global namespace across user config and all plugins.
Use read-only database credentials and scoped API tokens — never commit literal secrets into repo mcp_config.json files.
Pattern A (Single Project): commit AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/, and .agents/hooks.json directly (optionally referencing monorepo skills via .agents/skills.json).

Pattern B (Multi-Repo Team): package plugin.json, assets/logo.svg, rules/AGENTS.md, skills/, agents/, hooks.json, and mcp_config.json into one Git repo symlinked to ~/.gemini/config/plugins/<team-plugin>.
actionChecklist: Verify live MCP tools via Additional Options (...) -> MCP Servers.
Confirm all custom MCP server keys are team-prefixed and use least-privilege tokens.
Set up Pattern A (repo-local) or Pattern B (1-minute git clone + ln -s team plugin install) so teammates sync via git pull.

# Teammate 1-minute global toolkit install
git clone https://github.com/<org>/acme-antigravity-toolkit.git ~/tools/acme-antigravity-toolkit
ln -s ~/tools/acme-antigravity-toolkit ~/.gemini/config/plugins/acme-toolkit

# Stay in sync across all workspaces
git -C ~/tools/acme-antigravity-toolkit pull

steps.title: Senior Daily Operating Habits & Day-1 Onboarding Checklist
steps.summary: Setup delivers 40% of the value; the remaining 60% comes from disciplined daily session habits — Spec -> Build -> Independent Review -> /learn — plus a crisp Day-1 smoke test for every new teammate.
keyTakeaways: Run the 4-phase loop every day: Align (/grill-me -> /plan) -> Build (Agent Mode or /teamwork) -> Verify (clean-context Reviewer + 375/768/1440px /browser checks) -> Compound (/learn).
Master key slash commands: /plan, /grill-me, /boost, /teamwork, /goal, /compact (~65% context or 15–20 turns), /learn, /schedule, and /browser.

Enforce 5 Pro Context Hygiene Habits: (1) One session = one coherent deliverable, (2) Use explicit @ mentions, (3) Always decouple Author from Reviewer, (4) Persist state in .memory/ files not chat history, (5) Never fight the model twice on the same mistake — encode it via /learn.
Verify every Day-1 teammate with a live smoke test (run /plan + HITL trigger on engineering; run editorial-qa on content) and optional /schedule weekly hygiene automation.
actionChecklist: Day-1 [1/7] Install & Sign In: Install Antigravity 2.0 Desktop, Antigravity IDE, and agy CLI; authenticate with your team account.

Day-1 [2/7] Lock Global Safety Defaults: Set Tool Execution Policy = proceed-in-sandbox, Terminal Sandbox = Enabled, Non-Workspace File Access = ask, Internet Access = ask, and configure Command Allowlist/Denylist & Browser Allowlist.

Day-1 [3/7] Install Core Marketplace Plugins: Add team plugins via Customizations -> Marketplace (Google Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides/Canva/Figma for content; Cloudflare/Vercel/Supabase/Chrome DevTools for engineering) and sign in to each provider.
Day-1 [4/7] Link Team Toolkit Plugin: Clone and symlink your shared team plugin into ~/.gemini/config/plugins/<team-plugin> (or verify repo-local .agents/ discovery).
Day-1 [5/7] Verify Live Discovery: Open Skills & Customizations in Antigravity 2.0 (or run agy /help) and confirm all expected plugins, rules, skills, and MCP servers appear without errors.

Day-1 [6/7] Run Role Smoke Test: Engineering -> run /plan on a small task and verify sandboxed tests + HITL hook triggers; Content -> run editorial-qa on a sample draft and verify Google Docs/Drive connectivity.

Day-1 [7/7] Set Up 1 Recurring Automation (Optional): Use /schedule for one weekly team hygiene task (e.g., stale PR/CVE summary or content calendar check), run /compact around 15–20 turns, and update .memory/handover.md (<= 3 KB) on wrap-up.

    C --> D["4. Compound\n(/learn -> Rules & Hooks)"]

steps.title: Practical Loop Engineering: Goals (/goal), Schedules (/schedule) & Concurrency Caps
steps.summary: Operationalize Addy Osmani's 'Practical Loop Engineering' inside your daily Antigravity OS: distinguish finite Goals from recurring Cron Loops, cap concurrent agents at 3-5 so review quality stays sharp, and never let the generator grade its own homework.
keyTakeaways: Goals (/goal) vs. Loops (/schedule): Use /goal for run-until-done deliverables backed by an independent oracle (e.g., zero High/Critical CVEs + green cf-next-verify); use /schedule for recurring weekly hygiene sweeps (audit, handover size, manifest drift).
Respect the Human Review Ceiling (3-5 Concurrent Loops): Running 5-10 agent runs per day works smoothly when max concurrency stays <= 5; beyond that, review piles up and Dark Factory drift creeps in.

Never Let the Generator Grade Its Own Homework: Always split execution (cf-backend / cf-frontend) from clean-context verification (cf-reviewer / cf-tester / browser) so blind spots like mobile regressions are caught before merge.

Inspect skills/cf-loop-engineer/references/project-examples.md for 4 copy-ready Project_Antigravity recipes (Goal CVE convergence, Monday /schedule hygiene sweep, 4-worker Swarm, and Delegation Boundary table).
actionChecklist: Open `skills/cf-loop-engineer/SKILL.md` and `skills/cf-loop-engineer/references/project-examples.md` in the Live Repo Explorer.
Define an explicit machine-checkable oracle before launching your next `/goal` run.
Set up one read-only weekly `/schedule` hygiene loop checking CVE advisories, `.memory/handover.md` (<= 3 KB), and manifest drift.

codeSnippet.code:
/schedule every Monday at 09:00: Run a read-only Code Factory hygiene sweep:
1. Run `cd academy && pnpm audit --audit-level=high` for newly disclosed CVEs.
2. Verify `.memory/handover.md` <= 3072 bytes and `rules/AGENTS.md` <= 12 KB.
3. Check `generated-repo-manifest.json` against skills/, agents/, hooks/, courses/.
4. Report actionable P0/P1 drift items only; never auto-edit or git push.

prompts.title: Scaffold Engineering AGENTS.md & .agents/ Workspace
prompts.description: Generates a crisp, budget-safe engineering AGENTS.md (no YAML frontmatter, < 8 KB) plus .agents/hooks.json and starter skills tailored to your repo.
prompts.template:
Inspect `{{repo_path}}` and scaffold an Antigravity Pro Engineering Workspace:

1. Create a plain-Markdown `AGENTS.md` (no YAML frontmatter, <= 6 KB) documenting:
   - Exact Source-of-Truth commands for `{{tech_stack}}` (install, typecheck, lint, test, build).
   - Strict module boundaries (domain, API/boundary validation, UI tokens).
   - Non-negotiable security, reliability, and testing invariants.
2. Configure `.agents/hooks.json` with a fail-closed `PreToolUse` safety gate on `run_command` (always emitting explicit `allow` / `ask` / `force_ask` / `deny`).
3. Recommend the top 3 Marketplace plugins and project-level sandbox overrides (`proceed-in-sandbox` vs `request-review`) for this repository.
prompts.expectedOutcome: A committed, team-ready AGENTS.md and deterministic .agents/hooks.json configuration under the 24 KB / 20k-token rules budget.

prompts.title: Scaffold Editorial & Content Operations Workspace
prompts.description: Sets up a versioned content repository with brand-voice AGENTS.md, factual attribution invariants, and a decoupled editorial-qa SKILL.md.
prompts.template:
Scaffold an Antigravity Content Workspace for `{{brand_name}}` targeting `{{target_audience}}`:

1. Create directory structure: `content-briefs/`, `drafts/`, `published/`, and `.agents/skills/{draft-longform,editorial-qa,repurpose-kit}/`.
2. Write `AGENTS.md` encoding:
   - Brand voice: `{{voice_tone}}`
   - Banned AI cliches and filler intros.
   - Factual attribution invariant (mark any unverified stat with `[VERIFY: <claim>]`).
3. Create `.agents/skills/editorial-qa/SKILL.md` implementing the 4-stage audit (Accuracy -> Voice & Cliche Pass -> Structure & Readability -> Ready / Needs Revision verdict) designed for a fresh reviewer subagent.
prompts.expectedOutcome: A git-versioned editorial OS with enforceable brand voice rules and decoupled subagent QA.

prompts.title: Configure & Harden Team MCP Servers (Streamable HTTP)
prompts.description: Audits or generates a least-privilege mcp_config.json using Streamable HTTP, globally prefixed server names, and zero committed secrets.
prompts.template:
Design a clean `mcp_config.json` for `{{team_prefix}}` connecting `{{target_services}}`:

Constraints:
1. Prefix every server key with `{{team_prefix}}-` to avoid global MCP namespace collisions.
2. Use Streamable HTTP (`url` ending in `/mcp`) for remote servers; wrap any legacy `/sse` server via `mcp-remote` stdio bridge.
3. Never hardcode secrets — declare `${VAR}` placeholders with `variables` metadata (for plugin configs) or read-only credentials.
4. Provide verification steps using `Additional Options (...) -> MCP Servers`.

variables.label: External Services to Connect
variables.defaultValue: readonly analytics Postgres and internal docs CMS

prompts.expectedOutcome: A collision-free, least-privilege mcp_config.json compliant with Antigravity's Streamable HTTP transport.

prompts.title: Package an Org-Wide Git-Backed Antigravity Toolkit Plugin
prompts.description: Packages shared rules, skills, subagent personas, root-level hooks.json, and MCP configs into a single Git-symlinked team plugin.
prompts.template:
Package our team's shared standards into a standalone Antigravity plugin repo named `{{plugin_name}}`:

1. Create `plugin.json` (name, displayName, version `1.0.0`, description, logo, suggestedPrompts) and a clean square `assets/logo.svg` (>= 128x128).
2. Place consolidated invariants in `rules/AGENTS.md`, root-level `hooks.json`, specialized personas in `agents/*.md` (explicitly declaring `subagent: true`, `mainAgent: false`, and least-privilege `tools:`), and workflows in `skills/*/SKILL.md`.
3. Write a 1-minute `README.md` teammate install guide using `git clone` + `ln -s ... ~/.gemini/config/plugins/{{plugin_name}}` and `git pull` updates.
prompts.expectedOutcome: A portable, Git-versioned team plugin that keeps every engineer and content builder synchronized with git pull.

prompts.title: Run Day-1 Teammate Onboarding & Recurring Hygiene Smoke Test
prompts.description: Verifies a new teammate's Antigravity installation, sandboxed execution, HITL hooks, plugin discovery, and optional weekly /schedule job.
prompts.template:
Run a Day-1 Antigravity Pro Onboarding Smoke Test for a `{{role_track}}` teammate in `{{workspace_path}}`:

1. Verify discovered plugins, rules (`AGENTS.md`), skills, and connected MCP servers.
2. Confirm Global Safety Defaults (`proceed-in-sandbox`, Terminal Sandbox enabled, Allowlist/Denylist active).
3. Run a safe dry-run verification test (sandboxed read-only test command + confirm `PreToolUse` HITL hook triggers on a protected command pattern without executing it).
4. Propose 1 high-value weekly `/schedule` hygiene automation tailored to `{{role_track}}`.
prompts.expectedOutcome: Verified Day-1 setup with confirmed sandbox/HITL guardrails and a recurring team hygiene schedule.

prompts.title: Design a Bounded /goal, /schedule & Selective Autonomy Plan (cf-loop-engineer)
prompts.description: Applies Practical Loop Engineering to design a finite /goal with an independent oracle, a read-only /schedule hygiene loop, and a repo-specific Lights-Out vs. Human-Lit delegation matrix.
prompts.template:
Using `skills/cf-loop-engineer/SKILL.md`, design a Practical Loop Engineering operating plan for `{{repo_name}}`:

1. **Selective Autonomy Matrix:** Classify our routine tasks into **Lights-Out** (docs, tests, lint/type fixes, validated content bundles) vs. **Human-Lit** (auth, security/RLS, billing/finance, secrets/hooks, production deploys).
2. **Finite Goal (`/goal`):** Write a bounded `/goal` prompt for `{{goal_objective}}` with an independent machine-checkable completion oracle, a 3-retry circuit breaker, and a clean-context `cf-reviewer` grading step.
3. **Recurring Loop (`/schedule`):** Write a read-only `{{schedule_cadence}}` hygiene prompt monitoring CVEs, static rules budget, and `.memory/handover.md` drift.

variables.label: Bounded /goal Deliverable
variables.placeholder: Zero High/Critical CVEs + 100% green test/build suite
variables.defaultValue: Zero High/Critical CVEs + 4-course schema validation + green cf-next-verify

prompts.expectedOutcome: A concrete Delegation Boundary table, an oracle-backed /goal prompt, and a safe read-only /schedule hygiene automation.
